summary: Rear light of the Peche Island range pair, lit 1898 on the Lake St. Clair channel; its tower was moved in 1983 to Marine City, Michigan.

structures.note: Replaced 1983 by a modern structure; old tower restored at Marine City

access.note: Tower on the Marine City riverfront; closed to visitors (LighthouseFriends).

events.note: Front and rear range lights established 15 April 1898
Ice carried the range away in spring 1899; reestablished 26 April 1899
Tug carried away the front light on 27 July 1899; rebuilt at the owners' expense
Ice carried both clusters away in spring 1901; reestablished 29 April 1901
Permanent conical steel towers on concrete-pier cribs; rear light in operation 15 June 1908
Front light converted to acetylene; range automated; keepers assigned elsewhere
Crib superstructures rebuilt in reinforced concrete
Front range tower destroyed by acetylene explosion and fire on 5 Nov 1927 (the front tower, not this rear light)
Rear light replaced by a modern structure; old tower restored and placed on the Marine City riverfront, dedicated 21 August 1983
Tower repainted and fitted with new windows and lighting; cost about $35,000

wrecks.outcome: Carried away the front light; re-established 4 August 1899 at the expense of the tug's owners (Board report for the fiscal year ended 30 June 1900)

corrections.why: The 1928 Lighthouse Service Bulletin describes the front tower of this range as a conical structural steel plate tower, and LighthouseFriends describes the 1908 range towers as conical steel towers. The record's cast-iron entry for the rear range looks wrong.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The record gives 1970 and 1983. LighthouseFriends dates the replacement of the rear light to 1983. No source found here supports a 1970 deactivation.

notes_for_editor: Position: the USLHS place record gives 42.5893, -83.5287 for 'Peche Island Range Rear', about 85 km from the record's point and far from the channel; the archive's coordinates look wrong and the story does not use them. The record's point (42.716, -82.491) is the Marine City tower. The original range sat in shoal water north of Peche Island (LighthouseFriends), and no source here gives its coordinates. Dates: the record's 1921 'built' and 1970 'deactivated' events come from Rowlett's directory via the record; neither was found in the sources read here, so neither is in the story or the events list. The 1906 appropriation, the 1908 opening description (a Lake Carriers' Association quotation as printed by LighthouseFriends) and the 1940 electrification are from LighthouseFriends alone; the Light-House Board volumes for 1906-1915 are not in the corpus. Printed pages are not confirmed for the 1899 and 1901 Light-House Board reports, so the citations use scan pages. The 1899 volume has no OCR page index for the Isle aux Peches entry, so its page was found by text search at scan p. 217. The 1928 Bulletin account is on PDF p. 3; the explosion date appears in OCR as 'N ovem bel' 5, 1927, which is the exact text quoted. The fire account differs by source: the Bulletin says 'the city fire tug' responded; LighthouseFriends names a fireboat, the James R. Elliott, and says a fireman was thrown into the lake. The story does not name the fireboat or the fireman, which the sources do not reconcile. The Life-Saving Service 1884 table lists stranding places, not stations, and is used only for the Canadian location. Keepers: nine roster lines (USLHS). LighthouseFriends says John F. Kerby had six different assistants in his fourteen years; the roster's first-assistant lines for 1898 to 1912 are six, which agrees, and the story does not repeat the count. No keeper is linked to another station. Checked in this pass: the 1899 Board report (scan p.217) gives piles finished 20 April and the lights reestablished 26 April 1899; LighthouseFriends says the lights went back two days after the piles were driven (about 22 April). The story states both. The 1884 Life-Saving Service table is titled 'List of places on the Coasts of the United States where vessels have Stranded, during the last ten years' (not 1884 alone); the story says so. The 1908 rear-light description is the Lake Carriers' Association's, which LighthouseFriends prints; the story attributes it that way. Fire of 5 Nov 1927: the Bulletin names the city fire tug and the tender Thistle; LighthouseFriends names the fireboat James R. Elliott. The story states the difference and does not name a fireman. 'Grosse Point Flats' is spelled as LighthouseFriends prints it; the place is usually spelled Grosse Pointe. The 1901 Board entry is OCR-damaged at 'carried away by the [ice]' and the story does not quote that phrase.
